title: The Ember of the Glass Steppe Revisited
premise: When the border wards between the human realm of Thornfell and the fae Glass Steppe collapse on the night the stars go out, exiled storm-caller Wren Oyelaran discovers he is the last living signatory of the covenant that once held them — and that his exile was engineered by those who wanted the wards to fail. Hunted by a winter court that feeds on starless dark, Wren gathers a found family of smugglers, defrocked wardens, and a fae deserter to reforge the covenant at the Ember Shrine. The price of reforging demands a true name freely given, forcing Wren to claim the identity he fled. He sacrifices his storm-calling to relight the stars, ending the long winter but choosing a new life among the people who stayed.
about_author: Lior Eastwick is the pen name of a former mountain guide who writes fantasy shaped by real passes, weather, and the people who live off the map. Their work explores what justice looks like when no court will hear you.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Wren Oyelaran guides a smuggling run through the Thornfell passes when the border wards shatter and every star vanishes at once, plunging the mountains into unnatural dark. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: dread and disorientation as his carefully built exile life cracks open in a single night.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Buried
chapters.summary: Wren shelters with defrocked warden Sefa Ilori, who reveals records proving Wren's grandfather signed the original covenant — and that Wren's exile was arranged to remove him before it could fail. POV: alternating Wren and Sefa. Emotional beat: anger hardening into reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: A Deserter from the Winter Court
chapters.summary: The crew captures a fae scout, Ysolde, who defects rather than return to a winter court devouring its own people for warmth. She confirms the covenant can be reforged only at the Ember Shrine. POV: Ysolde. Emotional beat: wary empathy between enemies; first thread of found family.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Oath
chapters.summary: Wren calls in old debts across three freeholds, assembling a ragged company: smuggler captain Dov, hedge-witch Bramble, and Sefa's disgraced wardens. They swear an oath outside any law. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: cautious hope; the theme of justice beyond courts takes shape.

chapters.title: Frost on the Toll Road
chapters.summary: The winter court's riders ambush the company at a mountain toll, and Bramble is taken. Wren learns the court knows his name and wants him alive. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: grief and guilt; the cost of the road becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Court That Ate Its Own Light
chapters.summary: Infiltrating the winter court's ice-hold to rescue Bramble, Wren confronts Lady Vess, who claims his grandfather broke the covenant first — and shows him proof that complicates everything he believes. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the ground shifts under his identity; doubt replaces certainty.

chapters.title: Ember Shrine
chapters.summary: The battered company reaches the Ember Shrine, where the dying firekeeper explains the reforging requires a true name freely given by a covenant heir. Wren must stop running from who he is. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning; the choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Lady Vess assaults the shrine as the final snows begin. Dov falls holding the pass, and the shrine fire gutters to an ember as Wren steps forward to speak. POV: Ysolde. Emotional beat: sacrifice and terror at the story's darkest hour — the climax begins.

chapters.title: A Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Wren speaks his full true name — Wren Adeyemi Oyelaran, heir of both realms — and gives his storm-calling into the ember. The stars reignite one by one; the winter court unravels without its stolen dark. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: catharsis; identity claimed, not imposed.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: With the covenant renewed and no magic left, Wren chooses to stay in Thornfell with Sefa, Ysolde, and Bramble, rebuilding a border town where law never reached. Justice here is made by hand. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; found family endures.
